The story is unified and follows a clear, logical progression from the inciting tragedy to its long-term emotional aftermath. Recurring motifs—such as the snow, the unborn baby (and later, the demands of motherhood and daily life), and the mother's brass pin—bind the narrative together seamlessly. Every scene serves the central theme of how ordinary life, maternal instinct, and the quiet persistence of routine coexist with the lingering, unanswerable questions of a traumatic event. The rediscovery of the brass pin at the end brings the story full circle, providing a deeply resonant and satisfying conclusion.
